product.olivetti-m4-62.summary: The 33 MHz SX M4 in the 305 Box chassis.
product.olivetti-m4-62.history: The M4 Modulo range targeted professionals and sat between the personal-use PCS and the higher-performance M6 Suprema. In February 1994, MCmicrocomputer tested the M4-62 and listed it at 3,000,000 lire before VAT with a colour monitor.
product.olivetti-m4-62.warning: Partial T.1 motherboard emulation with the Olivetti 2.06 service BIOS.
product.olivetti-m4-62.architecture: Memory can grow without replacing the base RAM. The board has 4 MB soldered down, one SIMM socket and CL-GD5428 graphics.
product.olivetti-m4-62.verified: BluMach tested POST, floppy boot and VGA mode 13h with 4 MB of RAM and 512 KiB of video memory. The original Setup 1.04 saved CMOS in Standard mode. MS-DOS 5.00 booted from IDE after a power cycle with 85, 170 and 240 MB disks.
product.olivetti-m4-62.limitations: The 83C206Q and keyboard controller use compatible models. The factory BIOS, exact disk geometries and other board revisions remain unconfirmed.
product.olivetti-m4-62.service-guide: Olivetti, Personal Computer – Pocket Service Guide, vol. II, ch. 2
product.olivetti-m4-62.firmware: The family service package contains the Olivetti 2.06 BIOS and OVC 1.09 video firmware. The factory revision for this model remains unconfirmed.
product.olivetti-m4-62.creation.offer: 305 BOX · RAM 4 MB · VGA 512 KB · IDE 85/170/240 MB
product.olivetti-m4-62.source-brochure: Olivetti GmbH, M4-60/62/64/65/66 Modulo · Drucknummer 12129 · p. 2
product.olivetti-m4-62.creation.note: Place the 128 KiB service ROM at roms/machines/olivetti_m4_trota/EPROM.ROM.
The disk is created blank with a representative geometry. Use Olivetti Setup in Standard mode and install DOS from floppy.
